visual_inspection: PASS: twelve destination captures individually inspected; no label clipping, connector defects, caption overlaps, or page overflow.

html.heading: Appendix F — Running an Experimental Study: From Question to Credible Evidence

figures.alt: A vertical sequence asks what to learn, what to measure, what to compare, how large and uncertain the estimate is, and what the design justifies.
figures.caption: Figure F.1: Five questions connect an experimental design to the claim it can support. Revisit earlier steps when the evidence exposes a weakness.

figures.alt: A target population passes through random sampling into an evaluation sample and people outside the evaluation. Only the evaluation sample proceeds to random assignment and divides into treatment and control groups. Sampling is connected to external validity and assignment to internal validity; people outside the evaluation are distinct from the randomized control group.
figures.caption: Figure F.2: In this design, random sampling selects the evaluation sample from a target population; random assignment then divides that sample into treatment and control groups. Sampling supports population generalization, while assignment supports a causal comparison. Both require appropriate implementation and analysis.

figures.alt: Two assigned groups proceed through treatment receipt, outcome observation, and analysis. The diagram asks who received treatment and who was observed, and reminds the reader to track effects between groups.
figures.caption: Figure F.3: Assignment, treatment receipt, and outcome observation are different events. An intention-to-treat comparison keeps the original assignment groups while addressing missing outcomes and interference.
